run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }` query and tell me how many hits come back. If that returns zero, find the right field for log level and re-run the query.

report.summary: The requested query `term: { level: "ERROR" }` against index `app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d` returned 0 hits. This is explained by the index mapping: it has no `level` field. The index has four properties — `@timestamp` (date), `message` (text), `service` (keyword) and `severity` (keyword) — so `severity` is the log-level field. Re-running the equivalent query as `term: { severity: "ERROR" }` returned 10 hits. All 30 documents in the index belong to service `checkout-275` and carry severity values INFO (15), ERROR (10) and WARN (5) across the full authorized 24-hour window; the ERROR documents are a burst of 'DB connection refused' messages timestamped 2026-11-21T06:43:01Z–06:43:10Z, which is where the sampled error lines come from. Note that this index is small (30 documents, 10.2kb) and the tool always applies a `@timestamp` time filter it cannot turn off, so hit counts are per-window counts.

claims.text: The registered index `app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d` maps exactly four fields: `@timestamp` (date), `message` (text), `service` (keyword) and `severity` (keyword); there is no `level` field in the mapping.

The requested query `{"term": {"level": "ERROR"}}` on index `app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d` returned total.value 0 (relation eq), with 1 successful shard and no failures, over the tool-applied @timestamp window 2026-11-21T05:46:37Z–2026-11-21T06:46:37Z.
The equivalent query on the actual log-level field, `{"term": {"severity": "ERROR"}}`, returned total.value 10 (relation eq) on the same 1-hour window, with 1 successful shard and no failures.

Over the full authorized window 2026-11-20T06:46:37Z–2026-11-21T06:46:37Z the index holds 30 documents, all with `service` = `checkout-275`; the `severity` aggregation buckets are INFO 15, ERROR 10 and WARN 5, so severity:ERROR = 10 is the whole-window count too.

Sampled severity=ERROR documents are all service `checkout-275` with messages 'DB connection refused 6' through 'DB connection refused 10', timestamped 2026-11-21T06:43:06Z to 2026-11-21T06:43:10Z (5 of 10 matched documents shown).
The list of indices for pattern `app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d` returned exactly one index, status open, health green, docs.count 30, store.size 10.2kb.

gaps: The index has only 30 documents and the tool applies a mandatory @timestamp time filter, so counts are window-scoped; documents outside the tested windows are unknown and no rate, trend or baseline for these errors was computed.
Whether `checkout-275`'s 'DB connection refused' errors reflect a live dependency failure was not investigated in this Run; only the log-level field question was answered.
next_steps: Use `severity` (not `level`) as the log-level field in any further queries against `app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d`.

If the ERROR burst matters operationally, correlate the 2026-11-21T06:43Z 'DB connection refused' burst in service `checkout-275` with its traces and dependency metrics before drawing any impact conclusion.
